requirements.requirement: User-approved prospective doubling: newly started full generation/review cycles have a 21600-second (six-hour) overall cap. Phase planning targets are generation/build 3600 seconds, independent review 10800 seconds, correction/retest 5400 seconds, and exports/final QA/deployment 1800 seconds. Initial implementation has a separate 14400-second (four-hour) checkpoint, never charged silently to the generation lease. Two concurrent workers and two shared repair rounds remain unchanged. Phase/reviewer allocations are planning targets, not extra approval deadlines, and cannot extend the shared cap. Preserve all historical/current run deadlines, repair ledgers and failed/late verdicts; do not backfill historical timings or invent approvals. Every run, including success, failure, timeout, blocked and no-change, produces a user-visible budget report: observed elapsed versus allocated by phase and reviewer/task, remaining/overrun, outcome, coverage left unfinished, and an evidence-based more-allocation assessment with reason and any justified suggested extra time. Distinguish wall-clock phase/run time from aggregate overlapping worker time, and mark missing observations or assessments unknown rather than measured zero or completed. Include startup, queue/wait, tools, retries and finalization within the observed clock; expose untracked time. Distinguish time shortages from tooling/access/dependency/quality blockers; more time is not a cure for unavailable sandbox access. Recommendations affect future planning only, never silently extend a current run. This every-run notification requirement supersedes the former silent no-change policy without enabling model work, generation, commits or successful-input changes on no-change. Reports do not confer acceptance or activate scheduling.
requirements.enforcementScope: Prospective budget/reporting implementation and regression checks; historical records are untouched. New review/output features still require their own implementation and independent verification before accepted publication.
